content_html_sanitized:
“Alcohol Induced Deaths In The United States Increased by 89% from 1999 to 2024. The largest relative increase occurred among females aged 25–34, with a 255% increase, and males aged 25–34, with a 188% increase.”

See

Alcohol-induced deaths in the United States across age, race, gender, geography, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

These are really appalling numbers.

 

Why is MarijuanaNews.com reporting this? Better question, why isn’t this a headline on every media outlet that breathlessly reports every story about “Marijuana use linked to this or that”.

 

Where are the stories about how much stronger alcohol is today than back in the 1970s when everybody thought it was okay to drive drunk?  

 

Where are the stories about fetal alcohol syndrome?

See

The New York Post Can’t Figure Out Why Pregnant Women Use Cannabis. Perhaps Because They Are Not Getting Adequate Medical Care?

And

President Donald J. Trump, Whose Brother Died of Alcoholism, Withdraws Warning About Alcohol and Issues Study Favored by Alcohol Industry As He Considers Medical Cannabis Rescheduling

 

Why hasn’t The New York Post published a retraction and an apology for printing an editorial by Amanda Devine, saying, “Marijuana is a disaster. It’s infinitely worse than alcohol on every metric, especially mental health.”

 

Where are “addiction specialists” who warn against young people using drugs?

See

They Say The Brain Doesn’t Mature Until We Are 25 But That Doesn’t Stop The “Medical Profession” From Giving Children In Foster Care Powerful Psychiatric Drugs

 

When I say that the best two word explanation for Marijuana Prohibition is bad journalism, I am not just talking about what the media print, but also what they don’t print.

 

But let me be very clear that I am not advocating any kind of return to any form of Alcohol Prohibition.

 

On the contrary, I think that the legal age for alcohol (and cannabis) should be lowered from 21 to 18.

 

First, if they are  old enough to fight and die for their (my) country, then they are old enough to drink or smoke whatever. Besides, if they find out how badly we treat our veterans, they will need a drink.

See

The Wall Street Journal Carries Excellent Story About The Outrageous Medical Abuse of Veterans: But No Mention of Medical Cannabis

 

In the real world, many teens start drinking well before they are 21, even before they are 18. First, clearly the age limit laws are not working. Second, it is much better that they learn how to drink, and how not to drink, in an adult environment.

See Legalizing Alcohol Made Under Age Drinking Less Dangerous. Legal Cannabis Can Do The Same for Teens Illegally Toking and Vaping. The Dangers of Synthetic Cannabinoids

 

Do I expect this to happen? Well, don’t hold your breath, unless you take a toke first.
